BiblicalUsage: Pâram means to tear, to rend. After Nadab and Abihu die, Moses tells Aaron and his sons, Uncover not your heads, neither rend your clothes, lest ye die; and the leper in whom the plague is shall rend his clothes and bare his head and cry, Unclean, unclean.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the same tearing means opposite things: the priests must not rend in grief, and the leper must rend to confess his uncleanness — the law knows the difference.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
